answer: A reef of independent attesters can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent identity to be vouched for by several unrelated peers before it can transact. New identities start with a tiny trust pulse - a small, rate-limited allowance that grows only as the agent completes verified work and earns attestations. A bridge between separate trust clusters lets reputation transfer, but only when both sides' attesters agree, so an attacker spawning thousands of fake agents gains no shared trust and must pay real work costs for each one.
